content:
maria_h: Hey team — started seeing a big retry spike for the GPU inference service in us-west-2 around 09:10. App logs show repeated gRPC resets and higher tail latency, but node CPU/GPU utilization looks normal.

ajoy: Do we have per-endpoint connection counts? Could be ipvs skewing a small subset of pods.

maria_h: Pasting ipvs + endpoint view from one of the kube-proxy nodes:
```
# ipvsadm -Ln --stats
IP Virtual Server version 1.2.1 (size=4096)
Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
  -> RemoteAddress:Port           Forward Weight ActiveConn InActConn
TCP 10.32.8.14:8080 rr
  -> 10.32.9.3:8080               Masq    100    432      2
  -> 10.32.9.4:8080               Masq    100    14       1
  -> 10.32.9.5:8080               Masq    100    8        0
```

maria_h: Notice one endpoint has 432 active conns while others are tiny — that matches per-pod retries and hot-queues on that GPU pod.

devon: That pattern smells like connection persistence or hairpinning + asymmetric route. Any MTU/RDMA errors on the NICs? GPU nodes are on an mtu 9000 overlay.

maria_h: I pulled dmesg and saw repeated "mlx5: XDP RX drop" and some "TCP: Possible-Reorder" warnings on the same node. No obvious kernel panics though.

leo_k: Could be two factors: (1) ipvs scheduler hash bias when conntrack entries TTLs are reaped causing re-sharding, (2) an MTU mismatch causing retransmits that look like new flows so ipvs picks the same endpoint repeatedly. We recently enabled conntrack tuning on the nodepool.

ajoy: What are conntrack stats?

maria_h: ```
# conntrack -S | egrep "tcp.*established"
entries      : 82341	
established  : 48112
expire       : 600s (default)
```

maria_h: We also saw a kube-proxy roll last night with a config tweak (ipvs-scheduler changed to rr).

tess_oncall: Immediate mitigation: Can we cordon+drain the hot pod and let endpoints rebalance? Also bump conntrack timeouts to avoid frequent rehashes?

leo_k: Draining will shift connections but might be noisy. Short-term: retarget service to iptables mode on that node to remove ipvs scheduling for the service, see if the distribution evens out. Longer-term: capture tcp pcap on the node to confirm MTU fragmentation causing retransmit storms.

devon: I can run a quick iptables fallback on a single kube-proxy instance for the service: 
```bash
# edit /var/lib/kube-proxy/config.conf -> mode: "iptables" (for test)
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/kube-proxy -l nodepool=gpu-us-west-2 --grace-period=0
```

infra-bot: Scheduled action: kube-proxy rollout (test: iptables fallback) initiated by devon at 2035081240 for nodepool gpu-us-west-2.

maria_h: After switching one node to iptables we saw per-pod active conns flatten: the previously hot pod dropped from 432 -> 20 within ~30s, retries decreased.

ajoy: Good signal. Still need root cause though — logging an infra incident and an action item: capture MTU/rdma stats + tcpdump during next spike, and test kernel conntrack timeout adjustments.

maria_h: Filed INFRA-8476 with the captures attached. Next steps: schedule packet capture window, coordinate a controlled kube-proxy config change across the pool, and validate RDMA driver firmware on the affected nodes.

tess_oncall: I'll own the oncall runbook updates: add `ipvs -> iptables` quickfallover and the conntrack knobs to try before draining.

leo_k: One more datapoint — scheduler skew can be mitigated by enabling `source-ip-hash` for services that are sticky to clients, but that's a policy change. We'll discuss in postmortem.

maria_h: Thanks all — leaving the test iptables change running for now and collecting pcaps. Will post captures in the ticket when ready. :white_check_mark:
